text: I strongly believe that universal pre-K is one of the most important investments we can make as a society. Research from the Perry Preschool Project and the Carolina Abecedarian Project consistently shows that high-quality early childhood education leads to better academic outcomes, higher earnings, and lower rates of incarceration decades later. I recognize this is expensive — estimates for a national program range from $30 billion to $70 billion annually — and that implementation quality matters enormously. But the evidence is compelling, and I think the long-term return justifies the cost.
